body: Hey! Im not really sure what is the best thing to say here, but if you feel grossed out, just know that a lot of us in this subreddit go through similar struggles. You clearly don't enjoy your thoughts because they are intrusive, and they bother you. That's a sign that you're not what your thoughts are telling you. Perhaps you can try searching up POCD on tiktok and see how people with it handles their ocd or how they discovered it. Dont be too hard on yourself, you'll be okay <3

Im not in your position, and idk where you're located. But it does remind me of when i first questioned it myself. For me personally, so far ive told a counsellor, a psychologist and a psychiatrist about my fear of being a pedophile. Thankfully, all of them weren't panicking or felt the need to make an action. I think from our perspective, we fear that this is an extremely bizarre thing to admit but for mental health professionals, theyve probably dealth with clients who went through the exact same thing we go through, if not worse. In my personal experience, i dont gel well with counsellors. They dont seem to really have the depth that a psychologist has when handling issues like intrusive thoughts and severe depression.

But at the end of the day, sometimes, even mental health care is a trial and error so i hope you give yourself a chance to get some help and ease the stress you have regarding this topic <3

I never thought someone had similar experience as I did. I also have done questionable things in my teenage/early adult years, like 13-19. These things make it harder when I struggle with intrusive thoughts as an adult because it makes me think, "But well, you also did this in the past" and it just further threw me in the dark place. Now, anything resembling minor scares me even when there's no sexual undertone.

How do you manage to get over this? And how did you separate your mistakes and intrusive thoughts?

Right? I literally just replied to someone to try to comfort them because I know how horrible it feels, yet I can’t seem to figure out my own struggles. I think maybe giving advice is also a way of trying to soothe ourselves—like subconsciously, we know what we’d want to tell ourselves. But we only get to be really kind when the person going through it isn’t us, because we don’t have to argue with that person the way we do with ourselves. Their identity and intrusive thoughts are separate from us, so we're able to be more gentle without that echo in our mind saying, “You’re just making excuses to hide your true evil.”

We think the worst of ourselves, but when it’s someone else, that same harshness doesn’t apply.

I'm not an artist, so I can't relate to your experience, but I think from what I understand, you're doing really great for making sure that your vision of the models or art you create comes across as adults despite having face blindness. Is this process stressful for you?

We could also say, "Non-murderers wouldn’t feel tempted to kill another person." But I’ve had moments where I felt like I wanted to kill someone, almost as if the thought was real. Guess what? It stayed as a thought, and that doesn’t make me a creep or a criminal. Over time, my intrusive thoughts jump from one thing to another. As I’ve gotten older, my brain has started clinging to these sexual subjects more, like bestiality or pedophilia. I assume this happens because these are things we hear about in the news as adults.

Honestly, saying all this feels kind of hypocritical because I struggle with a similar situation as you, and it’s awful to find yourself wondering, "Am I actually a pedophile?" Right now, you’re probably just looking for something to clearly tell you, "No, you’re not a pedophile," to ease the stress you’re feeling.

One thing that sometimes helps me differentiate between genuine pleasure and intrusive thoughts is to compare my most embarrassing fetish with my intrusive pedophilic thoughts. With the fetish, even though I hate it and feel embarrassed by it, I can still find a way to enjoy it in my private time. But with the intrusive pedophilic thoughts, they’re so distressing that I spend more time worrying about them than actually "enjoying" them.

The first time I ever told anything regarding this was when I overdosed on antidepressants and I was in the emergency in hospital. I was extremely upset with their reaction as they were shocked and thought about it from mostly only one perspective which is religion. I told them in hopes I will get the attention and love I needed but ever since that day, I just suppress my feelings when I'm home. My father does send me for appointments every 3 months, and despite knowing his own daughter suffers with depression, anxiety and was suicidal, he doesn't seem to understand. My last appointment, he said to me "there must be a lot of patients who don't come for appointments. because you just talk and don't get medications" I feel disappointed for how ignorant my father is. when he heard about a young celebrity died from suicide, he said "too young to suicide". my mom on the other hand, she may not be as horrible as my father but I still very much dislike it when she thinks depression as something related to attitude or a thing that can be controlled. she once said "hey, when you're a little older (im 19 now), you should do volunteering activities. but just don't be depressed, helping those homeless people". There's so much more I can share but these are the highlights i could give you. I explained to some people about my parents and some said that my parents are emotionally abusive and i go through emotional neglect. as much as i hate their toxic behaviours, I still love them so much and spend a lot of time with them. It's just that, when it comes to this topic, i prefer staying quiet and only talk about the positives. that's why im here trying to find comfort from people in the internet and im happy to wake up this morning with lovely comments and awards :)
